Issued at 1137 AM CDT Sun Oct 18 2026

A southwesterly flow aloft was developing across southwest 
Kansas as an upper level ridge moves into the Mississippi Valley
and an upper low/trough begins to establish itself over the 
western United States. An upper level disturbance embedded in 
the southwesterly flow was located over southwest New Mexico 
earlier today and as this upper level wave crosses the Rockies 
and moves out into the Plains over the next 24 to 36 hours a 
weak surface boundary/cold front moves into portions of western 
Kansas by early Monday morning. At this time it appears there 
will only be an increase in clouds ahead of this approaching 
upper wave given limited moisture which will help keep 
temperatures up a some overnight compared to the last few nights
with lows tonight mainly in the 40s. On Monday little in the 
way of cooler air will accompany this weak cold front as it 
moves into western Kansas and becomes nearly stationary west of 
highway 83. High temperatures on Monday behind this front will 
be only a few degrees cooler compared to the highs on Sunday over the next 
 5 days.while further south and east (mainly across south 
central Kansas) the highs on Monday will be a few degrees 
warmer.

Warmer temperatures return to southwest Kansas next week. 
Ensembles are in good agreement today with an upper low 
deepening as it drops south along the West Coast early in the 
week. During the last half of the work week this upper low will 
begin to weaken as it moves across California and approaches the
four corners area. While this occurs the surface trough of low 
pressure will reestablish itself over eastern Colorado as 850mb 
warmer air develops and spreads east across western Kansas. 
Based on the latest ensembles the mean 850mb temperatures will 
warm from 10-15C at 7pm Monday to near 20C by 7pm Wednesday. 
These unseasonably warm temperatures are then forecast to 
remain in place through late week. This forecast warmup easily 
supports highs currently forecast in the 75 to near 80 degree 
range late week and may even end up being a few degrees warmed 
give the increasing southerly winds late week and deeper mixing 
potential being possible.

As for the increasing winds late week. Ensembles already 
indicated that deeper mixing will occur late week as a tight 
pressure gradient develops east of the deepening lee trough 
crossing eastern Colorado. All the ensemble clusters has the 
25th percentile of the 850mb winds Friday afternoon at around
30 knots and the 75th percentile at least 40 knots. The NBM 
already is forecasting that some areas west of highway 283 
(40-60% chance) could experience wind gusts in excess of 40 mph 
during the day on Friday. 

Cooler temperatures return next weekend along with a chance for
precipitation. The southwesterly flow aloft will continue 
across western Kansas through next weekend as the upper low over
California weakens and moves east towards the Central Rockies. 
Although there may be a chance (<20%) for widely 
scattered/isolated showers late Tuesday night as subtle upper 
wave embedded in the southwest flow crosses southwest 
Kansas...the better chance for precipitation will be from late 
Friday through the weekend as the main western United States 
upper trough approaches the area and improving moisture occurs 
ahead of this approaching upper wave based on PWATS increasing 
to greater than 80% across western Kansas and several days of 
improving IVT (Thursday night through the weekend). Friday night
the better chance for precipitation will be west of highway 283
but the chance for showers and thunderstorms will then spread 
across all of southwest and south central Kansas over the 
weekend as the upper level trough moves approaches western 
Kansas and a cold front drops south into the area. Along with 
the improving chances for precipitation this weekend there will 
southwest Kansas is in store for another shot of cooler air 
following the cold frontal passage.
